q-36749.name: Question 1
q-36749.problem:
If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 5 \\ -4 & -5\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =5,$
then what is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
q-36749.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =5.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 5 \\ -4 & -5\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 \\ -4 & -10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=0 \\ -4{x}_{1}-10{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 0 \\ -4 & -10 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-\frac{5}{2}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=2,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{-5}{2}=-\frac{5}{2}.$

q-18078.problem:
If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =1,$
then what is the value of $\frac{b}{a}?$
q-18078.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =1.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=6,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{a}=\frac{6}{-2}=-3.$

q-107107.name: Question 5
q-107107.problem:
If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 2 & 9\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3,$
then what is the value of $\frac{b}{a}?$
q-107107.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =3.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 2 & 9\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-3{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=-1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{a}=\frac{-1}{3}=-\frac{1}{3}.$

$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 \\ -6 & 4\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =10.$

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 \\ -6 & 4\end{aligned}]-10[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & -6 \\ -6 & -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-6{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0 \\ -6{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$

$$
-6{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-{x}_{2}.

$$
[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.

$$

q-107272.name: Question 8
q-107272.problem: Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}-23 & 6 \\ 8 & -10\end{aligned}]$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-7.$
q-107272.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =-7.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-23 & 6 \\ 8 & -10\end{aligned}]-(-7)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-16 & 6 \\ 8 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-16{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=0 \\ 8{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-16 & 6 \\ 8 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-16 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
-16{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{3}{8}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{8}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, setting ${x}_{2}=8,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 8\end{aligned}].
$$

q-18081.name: Question 10
q-18081.problem: Find an eigenvector  of $A=[\begin{aligned}8 & 4 \\ -10 & -6\end{aligned}]$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-2.$
q-18081.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =-2.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 4 \\ -10 & -6\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 & 4 \\ -10 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}10{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=0 \\ -10{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}10 & 4 \\ -10 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}10 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
10{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-\frac{2}{5}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{5}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, setting ${x}_{2}=5,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

q-107275.name: Question 11
q-107275.problem:
Given that $\lambda =-5$ and $\lambda =8$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 6 & 7\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
q-107275.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =-5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 6 & 7\end{aligned}]-(-5)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 6 & 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 6{x}_{1}+12{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 6 & 12 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-6){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=-2{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =8,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 6 & 7\end{aligned}]-8[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-12 & 2 \\ 6 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-12{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 6{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-12 & 2 & 0 \\ 6 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-12 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{6}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=6,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 6\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 6\end{aligned}].
$$

q-107311.name: Question 12
q-107311.problem:
Given that $\lambda =7$ and $\lambda =29$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}11 & -6 \\ -12 & 25\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
q-107311.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =7,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}11 & -6 \\ -12 & 25\end{aligned}]-7[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 \\ -12 & 18\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0 \\ -12{x}_{1}+18{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 & 0 \\ -12 & 18 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=\frac{3}{2}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=2,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =29,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}11 & -6 \\ -12 & 25\end{aligned}]-29[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-18 & -6 \\ -12 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-18{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0 \\ -12{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-18 & -6 & 0 \\ -12 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{2}{3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-18 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=3,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

q-107305.name: Question 13
q-107305.problem:
Given that $\lambda =3$ and $\lambda =10$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 2 & 9\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
q-107305.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 2 & 9\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=-3{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =10,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 2 & 9\end{aligned}]-10[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-6{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=2,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

q-80326.name: Question 14
q-80326.problem:
Given that $\lambda =0$ and $\lambda =11$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ 3 & 9\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
q-80326.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ 3 & 9\end{aligned}]-0[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ 3 & 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 0 \\ 3 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{3}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=-3{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =11,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ 3 & 9\end{aligned}]-11[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-9 & 6 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-9{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-9 & 6 & 0 \\ 3 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-9 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=\frac{2}{3}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=3,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

q-107306.problem:
Given that $\lambda =-2$ and $\lambda =17$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 20 & 13\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
q-107306.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =-2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 20 & 13\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 20 & 15\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ 20{x}_{1}+15{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 0 \\ 20 & 15 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=-\frac{3}{4}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{4}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=4,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =17,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 20 & 13\end{aligned}]-17[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-15 & 3 \\ 20 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-15{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ 20{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-15 & 3 & 0 \\ 20 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{4}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-15 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{5}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=5,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$
